Senses.Explanation: Baizhang’s wild fox names the canonical causality case and the fox-body at the center of its retelling. In the received account an old man says that his answer 'does not fall under cause and effect' led to five hundred lives as a wild fox. Baizhang answers the repeated question 'is not blind to cause and effect'; the old man reports release and asks for a monastic funeral. Guishan later responds to the raised story by shaking a door panel, and two monks dispute the easy fall-and-release opposition. Later masters repeatedly reopen the named case: Daxin raises it in the chamber, Wansong heads it as the eighth case, Foyan Qingyuan is tested on it, Shita Xuanmi Li comments on it in a hall address, Hongfu Ziwen versifies it, and Yunju Shuai'an Fancong gives another verse. A fox narrative thus becomes a stable public-case label; the entry reports its documentary parts and later testing without adjudicating cause and effect.
